utterance: The pattern of pain moving from your belly button to the lower right, loss of appetite, fever and tenderness strongly suggests appendicitis. There's also irritation of the lining inside your tummy. This needs hospital assessment by a surgical team now, because an inflamed appendix can burst. Please don't eat or drink while we arrange transfer, as you may need an operation. We can give pain relief with a small sip of water. Are you taking any other medicines or supplements, or do you have any liver problems?
reply: No, I'm not taking any other medicines or supplements. No liver problems.

utterance: I'll arrange ambulance transfer because of your significant pain and abdominal tenderness. Please don't drive yourself. I'll give you paracetamol now and ask the ambulance team to provide stronger pain relief and treatment for sickness if needed. We'll keep you here and monitor you until they arrive. At hospital they'll likely do blood tests and may do a scan, and the surgeon will decide whether you need surgery and antibiotics. We shouldn't delay transfer for blood tests or scans here.
reply: I don't want to be in the ambulance. I just want to go home.

utterance: I understand you'd rather go home. What worries you about the ambulance or going to hospital? Going home isn't safe with these findings—if the appendix bursts it can cause a serious infection and become life-threatening.

utterance: That's a reasonable alternative provided you go straight to emergency now, with your brother driving and staying with you. Please wait here for him. Do you agree to go directly to hospital rather than home?

utterance: I've arranged emergency department referral and handover for suspected appendicitis, including your fever, pulse, tummy findings and the pain medicine you've had. Your urine has tiny traces of blood and white cells, but that doesn't establish a urine infection or rule out appendicitis. Please keep avoiding food and drink until the hospital advises otherwise. If the pain suddenly becomes much worse or spreads across your tummy, you collapse, feel faint, become confused, or develop repeated vomiting while travelling, your brother should pull over safely and call 000. Don't wait to see if this settles, even if the pain briefly improves. We'll give you the referral details to take with you.
